title: SK hynix, Samsung push 16-layer HBM4 as Rubin favors 12
key_facts: Counterpoint Research said Friday (9 Oct) that most Rubin-based products will likely use 12-layer HBM4, not the eight-layer version rumoured.
This reverses Counterpoint's August report, which had pointed to an eight-layer HBM4 variant.
Making HBM can use more than three times the wafer capacity of conventional DRAM, so AI demand could keep standard memory supply tight.
SK hynix showed a 48GB 16-layer HBM4 at CES in January; Samsung has shipped 12-layer HBM4 since February.
A September report said SK hynix began volume shipments of 16-layer HBM4 for Rubin, but the company has not confirmed it.
Packaging capacity (TSMC's CoWoS) may limit finished AI accelerators even if memory is plentiful.
quote_evidence: Market researcher Counterpoint Research said Friday that most Rubin-based products will likely use 12-layer HBM4, the sixth generation of high-bandwidth memory, rather than the eight-layer configuration that had been rumored in the industry.
Counterpoint's latest assessment also marks a shift from its August report, which had pointed to Nvidia adopting an eight-layer HBM4 variant for Rubin.
Even with sufficient memory production, limited packaging capacity could constrain the supply of completed AI accelerators.
why_it_matters_hint: Analyst view eases fears of lower HBM demand; memory supply stays tight.
notes: Full text read at the Korea Herald. Counterpoint is the cited source of the forecast. An anonymous industry source is also quoted.
